title: Scaling of qubit coherence in quantum dot based Majorana chains: Rabi and Ramsey oscillations of Majorana qubits formed by four and six quantum dots
abstract: We present a theoretical study of the Rabi and Ramsey coherence time of Majorana-based qubits formed by double $N$-site quantum-dot artificial Kitaev chains, following the recent experimental realization arXiv:2607.09511. We generalize the qubit to two chains of arbitrary length and compare the Rabi and Ramsey oscillations of the four-dot and six-dot qubits, simulated with realistic disorder for three sets of parameters: small and large superconducting gaps, and the experimental parameters. We find that, in the pristine limit, the Rabi oscillation is independent of the chain length, whereas the Ramsey oscillation of the six-dot qubit suffers from larger leakage, because the third site suppresses the unwanted energy splitting away from the sweet spot but at the same time makes the deliberate splitting difficult to achieve, which requires a larger detuning that could excite the bulk. In reality with disorder, neither coherence time improves universally with the chain length. The Rabi coherence is set by the competition of three dephasing channels, and the additional dots pay off only if the fluctuation of the interchain tunneling is suppressed; the Ramsey coherence is set by the fluctuation of the energy splitting during the $σ_z$ rotation, which for the four-dot qubit is fixed by the sweet-spot disorder alone and does not depend on the mean splitting, whereas for the six-dot qubit the detuning that generates the splitting adds a fluctuation growing with the splitting itself, so the additional dots pay off only for small splittings. This implies that a longer chain is thus a better quantum memory but not necessarily a better qubit under manipulation. Although topological protection is expected in a longer Kitaev chain qubit, observing it in the current Rabi and Ramsey measurement protocols remains an experimental challenge.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes the coherence scaling of Majorana qubits built on quantum dot chains by examining Rabi and Ramsey oscillations for varying chain lengths. The authors find that while longer chains might improve quantum memory, the coherence time for qubit manipulation is not universally enhanced by increasing the number of dots due to complex disorder-induced leakage channels. The results highlight that coherence performance is critically dependent on precise parameter tuning rather than just system size.
main_problem: The study investigates how the coherence time (Rabi and Ramsey) of Majorana-based qubits scales as the number of quantum dots ($N$) increases in artificial Kitaev chains.
main_result: Increasing the chain length ($N$) does not guarantee better qubit performance; while longer chains might be better for quantum memory, the coherence enhancement is highly sensitive to disorder and specific manipulation protocols.
method: The authors employ theoretical modeling, deriving effective Hamiltonians and calculating coherence decay rates by analyzing leakage channels in both the pristine and disordered limits.
model_or_system: The system is a double $N$-site quantum-dot artificial Kitaev chain, designed to host Majorana zero modes. The physics is governed by a generalized Hamiltonian incorporating site energies, tunneling terms, and disorder.
key_observables: Rabi coherence time ($T_{2,	ext{Rabi}}$) and Ramsey coherence time ($T_{2,	ext{Ramsey}}$) oscillations, and the associated leakage probabilities ($P_{	ext{leak}}$).
important_parameters: Chain length ($N$), superconducting gaps, detuning ($\epsilon$), and the strength of disorder fluctuations.
main_assumptions: The analysis compares results for pristine limits versus realistic disorder, and the derivation of dephasing envelopes relies on Gaussian disorder assumptions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Rabi and Ramsey oscillations for $N=2$ and $N=3$ qubits in the pristine limit, comparing numerical and analytical results, and showing leakage probabilities.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical system and Hamiltonian, deriving the effective $2	imes 2$ block Hamiltonians for parity sectors, calculating the decay mechanisms for Rabi and Ramsey sequences, and finally analyzing the scaling effects of disorder.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the fundamental challenge of scaling quantum hardware: demonstrating that increasing physical size (more dots) translates into improved coherence for practical quantum computation protocols.
